**Accessibility**&nbsp;

These checks highlight opportunities to improve the accessibility of your&nbsp;

web app. Automatic detection can only detect a subset of issues and does&nbsp;

not guarantee the accessibility of your web app, so manual testing is also&nbsp;

encouraged.&nbsp;

**BEST PRACTICES**&nbsp;

\[user-scalable="no"\] is used in the \<meta name="viewport"\> element or the \[maximum-scale\] attribute is less than 5\.&nbsp;

**INTERNATIONALIZATION AND LOCALIZATION**&nbsp;

\<html\> element does not have a \[lang\] attribute&nbsp;

If a page doesn't specify a lang attribute, a screen reader assumes that the page is in the default language that PageSpeed Insights Copy Link Docsthe user chose when setting up the screen reader. If the page isn't actually in the default language, then the&nbsp;

~~screen reader might not announce the page's text correctly. Learn more about the lang attribute.~~&nbsp;

**NAMES AND LABELS**&nbsp;

Links do not have a discernible name&nbsp;

Link text (and alternate text for images, when used as links) that is discernible, unique, and focusable improves the navigation experience for screen reader users. Learn how to make links accessible.&nbsp;

**NAVIGATION**&nbsp;

Heading elements are not in a sequentially-descending order&nbsp;

Properly ordered headings that do not skip levels convey the semantic structure of the page, making it easier to navigate and understand when using assistive technologies. Learn more about heading order.&nbsp;
